newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern US corp bond deal to arrive soon.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern US corp bond deal to arrive soon.

text.p: A mega-debt offering from Norfolk Southern Corp is scheduled for arrival in the U.S. corporate bond market during the middle of this week, said market sources.

The $3 billion offering is expected to consist of tranches of five-year, 10-year, 30-year and 40-year, put seven-year securities. Merrill Lynch & Co and JP Morgan Securities will serve as joint-lead managers.
The company is widely expected to increase the size of the deal in order to tap positive bond market conditions and strong investor demand.
Norfolk Southern may issue up to $4.3 billion under a shelf filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Proceeds will be used to finance Norfolk Southern's acquisition of 58 percent of the assets of Conrail Inc for $6 billion.
Both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's downgraded the company's debt in anticipation of the higher leverage which would result from the acqusition.
The debt offering is currently rated Baa1/BBB-plus.
Sources said other high-grade issuers are likely to wait until the large deal is completed before tapping the market.
The new issue market for high-yield debt is expected to be very active this week with 13 new deals totalling roughly $2.5 billion in new supply expected to come to market.

The largest deals include a $470 million offering of four-year senior discount notes from a holding company of Coleman Co Inc and a $500 million offering of seven-year and ten-year notes from Owens-Illinois Inc.
William Scotsman Inc is also expected to sell $400 million in 10-year senior notes as part of debt refinancing in connection with a leveraged buyout of the company.
Record cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds, totalling $1.34 billion last week, are expected to generate positive market conditions for new deals.
"Buyers are flush with cash and they're not about to sell their bonds. So people have been looking to the new-issue market to invest," said one trader.
